heroHeadline: Venturella — Ex-GEO Group Executive — Officially Leads ICE as Senate Misses $71.7B Bill Deadline; Delaney Hall Curfew Defied
heroSubtitle: On June 1, 2026, David Venturella — a senior GEO Group executive who left ICE in 2012 to work for the private detention company that earns over $700 million annually in ICE contracts and operates Delaney Hall — officially became acting ICE director, succeeding Todd Lyons whose resignation took effect May 31. Civil rights advocates called the appointment unprecedented: the first time a leader from the private prison industry had been placed at the head of the agency responsible for funding and overseeing those contracts. Venturella inherits a record 73,000+ detainee population, an ongoing crisis at Delaney Hall — where Newark Mayor Baraka's May 30 overnight curfew was defied for a second consecutive night as protesters clashed with mounted NJ State Police who deployed tear gas against crowds that lit tires on fire — and a FY2026 custody death rate that has surpassed all prior annual records. The Senate formally missed President Trump's June 1 signing deadline for the $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation package, the largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history, with a floor vote still unscheduled as Byrd Rule disputes over the $1.776B DOJ anti-weaponization fund and $1B White House ballroom security line stall final Senate action. The 287(g) local enforcement partnership program reached 1,882 enrolled agencies as of May 31 — up 174% since January 2025.
